column1: # One row per behavioural claim in the spec trias (docs/meclaw-overview*,
# docs/cell-types*, docs/config*). Seeded 2026-08-21 out of the classified
# § 2.1) after every documentation strand of the remediation plan had landed --
# rows quote the text as it stands TODAY, not as the audit found it.
#   id             stable claim id. For `specified-not-built` it MUST end in
#                  `-de` / `-en`: the retraction is due in BOTH language
#                  versions, and the two languages cannot share one anchor
#                  string, so the pairing is expressed as twin rows.
#   doc            path from the repository root.
#   anchor         a fragment that must occur LITERALLY on ONE line of `doc`.
#                  Never include the marker itself in the anchor -- that would
#   test_or_issue  pinned: the test function name.
#                  specified-not-built: `GH #N`, the same N the marker names.
#                  built-unpinned: the issue that would produce the pin.
# Enforced by `scripts/check_claims.py`, run in CI (job `gates`). A commit that
# adds a behavioural promise to the trias adds its row in the same commit.
# Not in this file: statements of design intent ("hives are scope markers, not
# actors"). The target is what a reader could act on -- a message a cell
# answers, an operation, a field, an error code, a guarantee.
